topics.title: AI basics: what is AI and ML
topics.description: Artificial intelligence is the broad goal of building systems that perform intelligent tasks, while machine learning is a subset that learns patterns from data instead of relying only on hand-written rules.

lessons.title: What this topic clarifies
lessons.body: Artificial intelligence is the broad goal of building systems that perform intelligent tasks, while machine learning is a subset that learns patterns from data instead of relying only on hand-written rules. Focus on the boundary of this concept: what it includes, what it does not, and why that distinction matters when reading ML material.

lessons.title: Real-world framing
lessons.body: Use ai basics: what is ai and ml to translate a business question into a learning task. Write down the input available at prediction time and the exact output you need.

lessons.title: Common confusion to avoid
lessons.body: Learners often jump straight to algorithms. First confirm the problem type, data availability, and success metric; this prevents choosing the wrong modeling approach.

topics.title: Model interpretability

lessons.title: Metric strategy
lessons.body: Interpretability techniques such as feature importance and SHAP explain model behavior for trust, debugging, and compliance. Separate offline model quality from online product impact, and avoid optimizing one metric in isolation.

lessons.title: Error analysis
lessons.body: For model interpretability, review mistakes by segment (time, geography, class balance, user type) to uncover hidden risk pockets.

lessons.title: Decision policy
lessons.body: Define what metric values are acceptable for launch, what triggers rollback, and what evidence is needed before shipping a change.

topics.title: Deep learning architectures
topics.description: Different architectures specialize in different data modalities: CNNs for images, transformers for sequences, and recurrent variants for temporal patterns.

lessons.title: Representation learning
lessons.body: Different architectures specialize in different data modalities: CNNs for images, transformers for sequences, and recurrent variants for temporal patterns. Focus on how deeper layers progressively transform raw inputs into task-relevant features.

lessons.title: Training stability
lessons.body: In deep learning architectures, monitor optimization signals (loss trends, gradient behavior, overfitting gap) instead of only final accuracy.

lessons.title: Practical trade-offs
lessons.body: Balance performance with compute cost, latency, and data requirements; the best architecture is task-dependent, not universally bigger.
